stroomoverschot.intro: What should you do with surplus solar energy? Feeding it back to the grid is not always possible anymore and can even cost money. Lemnion stores your surplus in a battery, for your own use at the right moment.
stroomoverschot.s1h: Solar panels produce too much and that costs money
stroomoverschot.s1p: Hotels with large roof surfaces often generate more solar energy than they consume directly. Feeding back to the grid used to be the solution, but those days are over. More and more energy suppliers charge feed-in fees, the net-metering scheme is being phased out, and on sunny days the electricity price is sometimes negative. You generate power, feed it back, and pay for it. It can be done differently.
stroomoverschot.f1p: Your solar panels generate plenty of power during the day, often more than the hotel consumes at that moment.
stroomoverschot.f2p: Feeding back to the grid increasingly costs money. Penalties, feed-in fees, negative electricity prices.
stroomoverschot.f3p: Store the surplus in your Lemnion battery. Use it in the evening during the peak, or charge guests' cars with it.
stroomoverschot.c1p: Lemnion connects solar panels directly to the battery's DC bus, without conversion losses. Every kWh generated enters your battery with maximum efficiency.
stroomoverschot.c2p: The EMS decides in real time: store in the battery, use directly in the hotel, or charge guests' EVs. Always the most profitable choice.
stroomoverschot.c3p: With solar and storage combined, typical hotels cover most of their electricity needs from their own installation. This makes them independent of the grid.
stroomoverschot.ctah: Ready to free your hotel from grid congestion?
stroomoverschot.ctap: Calculate within 1 minute what your hotel can save with its own energy system.
